title: Droughts worsen air quality and health by shifting power generation
abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a leading environmental cause of mortality. Droughts can worsen air quality in regions that rely on hydropower by shifting energy production to combustion power plants. This study quantifies drought-induced excess PM2.5 in Latin America and the Caribbean, where over 443 million people live within 50 km of a combustion power plant. Leveraging a monthly plant-level panel spanning 20 years, we link hydrological droughts, measured as negative runoff anomalies in hydropower watersheds, to changes in PM2.5 concentrations near combustion power plants. Our analysis reveals that these droughts lead to an average increase of 0.83 μg m−3 in PM2.5 levels. Counterfactual simulations for the region reveal that this excess PM2.5 results in up to 10,000 premature deaths annually. Combining our estimates with climate, demographic, and combustion power plant phase-out projections, we demonstrate that this health burden will persist over the next four decades without targeted interventions.
abstract_zh: 细颗粒物（PM2.5）是导致死亡的主要环境因素之一。在依赖水电的地区，干旱会将发电转向燃烧类电厂，从而恶化空气质量。本研究量化了拉丁美洲和加勒比地区干旱所导致的额外PM2.5，该地区有超过4.43亿人居住在距离燃烧类电厂50公里范围内。利用为期20年的月度电厂层面面板数据，我们将水文干旱（以水电流域径流负异常衡量）与燃烧类电厂附近PM2.5浓度的变化联系起来。分析表明，这些干旱平均使PM2.5浓度增加0.83 μg/m³。针对该地区的反事实模拟显示，这些额外的PM2.5每年可导致多达10,000人过早死亡。结合气候、人口以及燃烧类电厂淘汰计划的预测，我们表明，若不采取针对性干预，这一健康负担将在未来四十年内持续存在。

title: Household Financial Decision-Making After Natural Disasters: Evidence from Hurricane Harvey
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
abstract: We study household credit responses to Hurricane Harvey using new, geographically granular data on credit cards, mortgages, and flooding. Estimates from a differences-in-differences design that exploits the flooding gradient show that affected households only borrow at low-interest rates, often using promotional (zero interest) cards and that they quickly pay down balances. We also document that take-up of forbearance (borrowing by missing mortgage payments without penalty) increases with flooding. These results are attenuated in floodplains, particularly in structures subject by code to physical hardening. Our results indicate that credit acts as a substitute for the lack of physical hardening.
abstract_zh: 我们利用新的、地理粒度较细的信用卡、抵押贷款和洪水数据，研究家庭对飓风哈维的信贷反应。利用洪水梯度的双重差分设计所得估计表明，受影响家庭仅以低利率借款，且常使用促销（零息）信用卡，并很快偿还余额。我们还记录到，随着洪水加重，利用宽限期（即不受罚地拖欠抵押贷款还款而借款）的比例上升。这些结果在洪泛区有所减弱，尤其是在依据规范必须进行物理加固的建筑中。我们的结果表明，信贷是对物理加固缺失的一种替代。

Mangroves Protect Coastal Economic Activity from Hurricanes
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: This paper evaluates whether mangroves can mitigate the impact of hurricanes on economic activity. The paper assembles a regionwide panel dataset that measures local economic activity using nightlights, potential hurricane damages using a detailed wind field model, and mangrove protection by mapping the width of mangrove forests on the path to the coast. The results show that hurricanes have negative short-run effects on economic activity, with losses likely concentrated in coastal lowlands that are exposed to both wind and storm surge hazards. In these coastal lowlands, the estimates show that nightlights decrease by up to 24% in areas that are unprotected by mangroves. By comparison, the impact of the hurricanes observed in the sample is fully mitigated in areas protected by mangrove belts of 1 km or more.
abstract_zh: 本文评估红树林能否减轻飓风对经济活动的影响。本文构建了一个区域性面板数据集，利用夜间灯光衡量当地经济活动，利用详细的风场模型衡量潜在的飓风破坏，并通过绘制通往海岸路径上红树林的宽度来衡量红树林的保护作用。结果显示，飓风对经济活动具有负面的短期影响，损失可能集中在同时面临风力和风暴潮灾害的沿海低地。在这些沿海低地，估计显示，在无红树林保护的地区，夜间灯光最多下降24%。相比之下，在有1公里或以上宽度红树林带保护的地区，样本中所观察到的飓风影响被完全抵消。
